target.title: fix(vydra): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Vydra media generation would not get their configured provider request policy applied when the generation service is reached through the shared Vydra HTTP path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vydra submit/download flow now builds its HTTP resolver from the configured provider request policy, so custom headers, proxy dispatchers, and private-network policy are carried into the generated media requests. The change stays inside the Vydra shared request setup and does not change model parameters or result parsing.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

Users and operators can rely on the same request policy they configured for the provider when Vydra generates images or videos, including controlled network routing and required outbound headers.

## Evidence

### 2026-07-13 controlled local Vydra-compatible HTTP proof

- Exact PR head tested and pushed: `6ce5e81ba2383cf154254d6c02b1e5c597c29df3`.
- Scope: controlled local Vydra-compatible HTTP endpoint on `127.0.0.1`, using real `global fetch` through the provider image/video paths. This is stronger than the earlier mocked-fetch proof, but it is not a live Vydra API call.
- Added proof coverage:
  - image flow: POST `/api/v1/models/grok-imagine`, GET `/api/v1/jobs/job-local-image`, GET `/generated/local-image.png`
  - video flow: POST `/api/v1/models/veo3`, GET `/api/v1/jobs/job-local-video`, GET `/generated/local-video.mp4`
  - both submit and poll requests carried the configured `X-Vydra-Policy` header, with `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` and a local private endpoint base URL.
  - both flows returned completed generated media through the provider helpers.
- Commands run:

  ```bash
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vydra/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/vydra/video-generation-provider.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --write --threads=1 extensions/vydra/provider-test-helpers.test.ts extensions/vydra/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/vydra/video-generation-provider.test.ts
  git diff --check
  ```

- Result:

  ```text
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  16 passed (16)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 44.45s
  Finished in 15ms on 3 files using 1 threads.
  git diff --check passed
  ```

- Not tested / remaining review gap: no live Vydra account, external proxy, TLS route, or real generated Vydra media artifact was exercised. The new evidence is local representative HTTP behavior and should not be represented as live-provider proof.

### Original focused regression proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vydra/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/vydra/video-generation-provider.test.ts`
- Result: 2 test files passed, 14 tests passed before the local HTTP harness was added.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD --`
- Result: passed.

target.title: fix(usage): ignore invalid Z.ai reset timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Z.ai usage fetch converts `nextResetTime` with `new Date(...).getTime()`. Invalid strings produce `NaN`, which is then stored on the usage window as `resetAt` and can poison downstream reset/cooldown logic that expects a finite timestamp or an unset value.

This is provider-contract hardening at the Z.ai usage parser boundary: untrusted quota metadata must not introduce non-finite numbers into domain objects.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts`, keep `resetAt` only when `Number.isFinite(parsedReset)` so invalid reset strings are ignored while valid ISO timestamps still populate `resetAt`.

## User Impact

**Before:** Invalid `nextResetTime` values could yield `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows.
**After:** Invalid reset strings leave `resetAt` undefined; valid ISO resets still work.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/zai-invalid-reset-time` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `ed45a4bf` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > ignores invalid nextResetTime while preserving valid ISO resets
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

### Diff summary

```
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts       | 4 +++- (finite reset guard)
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts  | 42 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ (invalid reset regression)
```

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Invalid truthy `nextResetTime` no longer becomes `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows; valid ISO resets still populate finite `resetAt`. Live authenticated Z.ai usage calls also flow through the same production `fetchZaiUsage` path.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, worktree `codex/zai-invalid-reset-time` at `ed45a4bf`; live `ZAI_API_KEY` against `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` via production `fetchZaiUsage` (`node --import tsx`).
**Steps run after the patch:**
1. Call production `fetchZaiUsage` with a live Z.ai/BigModel API key (key not logged).
2. Separately call production `fetchZaiUsage` with a Response whose limits include `nextResetTime: "not-a-date"` and a valid ISO monthly reset to prove the finite-guard path.
**Evidence after fix:**

Live authenticated usage call (redacted; account has no coding plan):

```text
{
  "provider": "zai",
  "displayName": "z.ai",
  "error": "current user does not have a coding plan",
  "windows": []
}
```

Parser hardening on the same production function (invalid + valid resets):

```text
main-style parse: nextResetTime="not-a-date" -> getTime=NaN (Number.isNaN=true)
after fix via fetchZaiUsage:
  Tokens (6h): usedPercent=32, resetAt=<undefined>, resetAtIsFinite=false
  Monthly: usedPercent=12.5, resetAt=1767830400000, resetAtIsFinite=true
```

**Observed result:** Live Z.ai accepted the key and returned a structured usage error through production `fetchZaiUsage` (empty windows because this account has no coding plan). On the same production parser path, invalid `nextResetTime` is dropped and valid ISO `resetAt` remains finite.
**Not tested:** A live quota payload that actually contains an invalid `nextResetTime` string. This account returns the coding-plan missing error with empty windows. Incidence of invalid upstream reset strings remains unverified; the change is parser-boundary hardening plus live path smoke.

target.title: fix(clawhub): validate content-length with parseMediaContentLength
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/clawhub.ts` uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` to parse the Content-Length response header — the same pattern that was replaced in `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` by #105954. Unlike `parseMediaContentLength` (from `@openclaw/media-core/content-length`), `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` does not validate comma-separated or duplicate Content-Length values, nor does it reject values outside `Number.isSafeInteger`. A malformed header passes through as a parsed number instead of being rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt `parseMediaContentLength`, the same shared helper that #105954 already validated for camera downloads. This is the only remaining `src/` call site that parses a Content-Length header with `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`.

## User Impact

Malformed Content-Length headers from ClawHub responses are now rejected with a clear error. Valid headers are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/clawhub.ts` — replaced `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` with `parseMediaContentLength`; adjusted `undefined` check to `null`
- `packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts` — existing tests for the helper
- `pnpm test src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — 69 passed, 0 regressions
